chosen.premise: Nidoking’s horn is hard enough to pierce diamond, but it also contains venom.
chosen.hook: Nidoking’s horn can pierce diamond—and it’s poisonous.
chosen.visualIdea: Show the horn drilling through a diamond, then reveal a venom warning over the same horn.
chosen.note: A distinctive two-part contradiction: the horn can pierce diamond, yet it is also venomous. Every part of the hook is directly supported and visually clear.

candidates.premise: Nidoking’s tail can topple a metal transmission tower with one swing.
candidates.hook: This Pokémon can knock down a transmission tower with its tail.
candidates.visualIdea: Animate Nidoking swinging its tail into a metal transmission tower as it collapses.
candidates.note: A highly concrete destructive feat, directly supported by two Pokédex entries and easy to visualize. The general strength angle is less exclusive to Nidoking.

candidates.premise: Nidoking is impossible to control during a rampage, yet calms around a long-time Nidoqueen companion.
candidates.hook: Nothing can stop Nidoking—except one Pokémon it knows well.
candidates.visualIdea: Cut from a raging Nidoking to the same Pokémon visibly calming beside a familiar Nidoqueen.
candidates.note: The emotional reversal is unusually specific and memorable. The Sword entry supports the exception, though “nothing can stop it” and the exact relationship are slightly broader than the evidence.

candidates.premise: Nidorino reaches level 16, but Nidoking only appears when a Moon Stone is used.
candidates.hook: Nidoking doesn’t evolve at a higher level—it needs a Moon Stone.
candidates.visualIdea: Display Nidorino at level 16, then freeze the level counter while a Moon Stone triggers evolution.
candidates.note: A clean, game-mechanic explanation with strong on-screen potential, but experienced players are unlikely to find the evolution method surprising.

candidates.premise: The Moon Stone changes Nidorino from pure Poison into Nidoking’s Poison/Ground typing.
candidates.hook: One Moon Stone adds an entire second type to Nidorino.
candidates.visualIdea: Show a Poison-only Nidorino gaining a Ground-type color and a second type label after evolution.
candidates.note: Accurate and easy to show, but gaining a second type on evolution is not especially unusual, and the premise lacks a sharper contradiction or benchmark.

candidates.premise: Nidoking’s signature fighting style uses its thick arms, legs, and tail for close-range attacks.
candidates.hook: Nidoking isn’t just a horn fighter—it specializes in melee combat.
candidates.visualIdea: Highlight Nidoking’s arms, legs, and tail one by one, then show a close-range combo.
candidates.note: Well supported, but it is primarily a broad combat description. Many physically oriented Pokémon could use the same angle.
